study type: Retrospective cohort study / Analysis of linked population data
exposure: Maternal cigarette smoking (timing by trimester and intensity level)
cohort: The study included 2,485,743 singleton births drawn from the 2010 National Center of Health Statistics (NCHS) linked birth/infant death file of US residents in 33 states.
finding: Maternal smoking at both high and low intensity during the first and second trimesters was associated with significantly higher odds of preterm birth compared to smoking only in the first trimester, identifying a vulnerability window.
